content:
Ashley: Quick heads-up — I ran a focused microbench comparing two KV cache strategies: 
1) slab-reserve: preallocate workspace slabs per-request to avoid on-the-fly allocations
2) thin-evict: smaller per-request caps + more aggressive eviction and compaction

Ben: TL;DR? :eyes:

Ashley: Short summary: slab-reserve improves p99 latency by ~20–30ms on long-seq workloads, but we observed ~2.5x higher memory fragmentation and a couple of transient OOMs under mixed-size traffic. thin-evict has slightly higher median latency but far fewer OOMs and lower overall GPU footprint. Full numbers below.

Maria: hmm kernel selection could amplify that. If reserved slabs push a different gemm/kernel path for long sequences we might be seeing runtime memory spikes + unexpected workspace blowup. Did you capture kernel / allocator events?

Ashley: Yep. Here's an excerpt from the profiler (trimmed):

```
# bench=reserve, seq=1024, batch=8
alloc_count: 1842
free_count: 1801
frag_pct: 27.4
kv_hit_rate: 0.72
p50_latency_ms: 42.1
p95_latency_ms: 89.3
p99_latency_ms: 132.7
kernel_path: cuda_gemm_fast (fallbacks: cuda_gemm_standard)
OOM_events: 2 (both on mixed-size bursts)

# bench=thin-evict, seq=1024, batch=8
alloc_count: 1320
free_count: 1312
frag_pct: 8.9
kv_hit_rate: 0.68
p50_latency_ms: 46.4
p95_latency_ms: 94.1
p99_latency_ms: 160.5
kernel_path: cuda_gemm_standard
OOM_events: 0
```

Ben: Interesting — reserve reduces p99 but frag_pct is alarming. Any idea why alloc_count is so much higher?

Ashley: The allocator is doing more small slab allocations when we reserve per-request workspace. That increases internal fragmentation because KV entries are many small blocks. When kernel switches to the fast GEMM path, it requests larger contiguous workspace which triggers eviction and occasional OOM when fragmentation prevents satisfying the allocation.

Jordan: Can you run a trace with per-request cap + relaxed prefill? Maybe a hybrid: reserve a small hot-slab + let decode prefill use ephemeral buffers. Command I used in the sim harness: 

```bash
./kv_bench --mode=hybrid --reserve-hot=64KB --per-request-cap=256KB --evict-policy=age-lru --trace=allocs.json
```

Ashley: Will run that. Also trying an alternate allocator coalesce patch which delays free-to-backlist for 10ms to allow quicker coalesces — should reduce fragmentation.

Maria: Also measure impact on kernel selection thresholds. If we can bias sequence-length histogram to keep gemm_standard 90% of time, we might trade a little throughput for far fewer OOMs. Worth exploring.

Ben: OTOH customers with strict p99 SLOs might prefer the reserve approach if we can fix fragmentation. Can we try coalesce + bigger contiguous pool for kernel-hungry ops?

Ashley: Plan: 1) run Jordan's hybrid bench today and attach traces (A) 2) test allocator coalesce patch in sim cluster (B) 3) add a tiny runtime flag to prefer standard kernel when fragmentation > 15% to avoid cross-allocation pressure (C)

Jordan: SGTM. If (B) reduces frag_pct to <12% without hurting p99 too much, we can A/B on a small canary GPU pool. I'll set up the canary job.

infra-bot: Deploy job queued: kv-bench-hybrid-210 -> cluster/sim-canary (resources requested: 2xA100). CI: pass -> will start in 12m.

Ben: Cool — please add a one-line summary to the perf board when you have results. Also add the raw alloc trace to the issue so SRE can correlate with eviction logs.

Ashley: Will do. I'll drop allocs.json + kernel traces here when ready. Thanks! :thumbsup:
